questions.stem: SUFISM in India was primarily organised into SILSILAS (orders). The most popular silsila in medieval India was the:

options.option_text: CHISHTI — founded by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti at Ajmer; embraced poverty, music (sama), and openness to all faiths

questions.explanation: SUFISM — mystical Islamic tradition emphasising LOVE of God (ishq), inner purification (tasawwuf), self-annihilation in God (fana), + union with the Divine (baqa). Entered India via Central Asia in the 12th-13th c. Organised into SILSILAS — mystical orders traced via a CHAIN (silsila) of spiritual transmission from the founder back to Prophet Muhammad. FOUR MAIN silsilas in medieval India: (1) CHISHTI — founded in Herat by Abu Ishaq Shami; brought to India by KHWAJA MOINUDDIN CHISHTI (1141-1236), who settled at AJMER (~1195); most POPULAR order; accepted poverty, sama (musical assembly), open-door policy for Hindus + low-castes + women. Famous saints: Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer), Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Delhi), Baba Farid (Pakpattan, Punjab), NIZAMUDDIN AULIYA (Delhi), AMIR KHUSRAU (disciple of Nizamuddin, father of Qawwali), Nasiruddin Chirag-e-Dilli, Shaikh Salim Chishti (Fatehpur Sikri). (2) SUHRAWARDI — brought by Bahauddin Zakariya to Multan; accepted state patronage; more aligned with orthodoxy. (3) QADIRI — later entry (15th-16th c., Dara Shikoh's order). (4) NAQSHBANDI — orthodox order; entered via Baqi Billah in 16th c.; Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi (Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani) was a Naqshbandi who opposed Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi. CHISHTI SHRINES are still the MOST VISITED — Ajmer attracts millions.

questions.stem: KHWAJA MOINUDDIN CHISHTI, founder of the Chishti order in India, is buried at the famous dargah in:

options.option_text: AJMER SHARIF (Rajasthan) — one of the most visited shrines in India; pilgrimage (ziyarat) attracts millions, Muslims + Hindus alike

questions.explanation: KHWAJA MOINUDDIN CHISHTI (1141-1236), also called 'GHARIB NAWAZ' ('Benefactor of the Poor'). BIRTH in Sistan (modern Iran/Afghanistan); migrated to India in late 12th c., settled in AJMER (~1195, during Prithviraj Chauhan's rule; some accounts differ). Preached love-based Islam, mystical union, rejection of worldly attachments. Died 1236 at Ajmer, age 97. TOMB — AJMER SHARIF DARGAH — built in 1240s; continuously patronised by Mughal emperors: (a) AKBAR walked BAREFOOT from Agra to Ajmer (Nov 1570, a 14-day pilgrimage) to offer thanks for the birth of Salim (later Jahangir); (b) BUILT a cauldron (Kalan Deg) in the dargah for communal meals; (c) Jahangir's wife Nur Jahan also visited. URS: 6-day annual festival on the anniversary of his death (Rajab month) — up to 4-6 lakh pilgrims. Interfaith character: the dargah welcomes people of all faiths; Hindu-Muslim composite culture icon. PM + CM often send chadars (offerings) to Ajmer. DARGAH HIERARCHY of CHISHTI saints + shrines: (1) Ajmer (Moinuddin); (2) Delhi — Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Mehrauli, near Qutb Minar); (3) Pakpattan (now in Pakistan) — Baba Farid; (4) Delhi — NIZAMUDDIN AULIYA (largest shrine complex in Delhi, also where Amir Khusrau + Mirza Ghalib are buried); (5) Fatehpur Sikri — Salim Chishti (white marble tomb inside Buland Darwaza complex).

questions.stem: AMIR KHUSRAU (1253-1325), the 'PARROT OF INDIA' (Tuti-e-Hind), was a disciple of which Sufi saint?

options.option_text: NIZAMUDDIN AULIYA — the celebrated Chishti saint of Delhi; Khusrau's tomb lies beside Nizamuddin's dargah

questions.explanation: AMIR KHUSRAU (1253-1325) — the most celebrated multilingual Indo-Persian poet-musician of medieval India. BIRTH: Patiyali, UP (father was a Turkic noble, mother an Indian Muslim). Served in the courts of 7 SULTANS (from Balban to Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) — longest court career of any poet. DISCIPLE of NIZAMUDDIN AULIYA (~1238-1325) — the great Chishti saint of Delhi; Khusrau's devotion to his pir was legendary. Both died within 6 months of each other in 1325; Khusrau is buried at the same DARGAH COMPLEX of Nizamuddin in Delhi (his tomb adjacent to the master's). LITERARY CONTRIBUTIONS: (1) 'TUTI-E-HIND' (Parrot of India) — title for his unmatched Persian + Hindavi poetry; (2) pioneered HINDAVI (early Urdu/Hindi) literature; earliest known 'Pahelis' (riddles) + 'Mukarniyan' (poetic games) + 'Dohas' in Hindavi. (3) Wrote 8 books including Khamsa-i-Khusrau (5 romances incl. Shirin Khusrau, Laila Majnun), Miftah-ul-Futuh, Nuh Sipihr, Tughlaqnama. MUSICAL CONTRIBUTIONS: (1) Invented QAWWALI — devotional Sufi music (Allah-hoo; his most famous is 'Man Kunto Maula'). (2) Credited with inventing several ragas (Yaman, Sarparda, Zilaph) + the SITAR + TABLA (debated — instruments actually evolved later but in his tradition). FAMOUS LINES: 'Agar firdaus bar roo-e-zameen ast / hameen asto, hameen asto, hameen ast' ('If there is heaven on earth — it is here, it is here, it is here') — about KASHMIR.

questions.stem: The concept of WAHDAT-UL-WUJUD (Unity of Being) in Sufi philosophy means:

options.option_text: ALL existence is ONE — there is no being other than God; the phenomenal world is a manifestation of the Divine

questions.explanation: WAHDAT-UL-WUJUD ('Unity of Being') — a central metaphysical doctrine in Islamic mysticism, propounded most systematically by the Andalusian Sufi IBN ARABI (1165-1240). CORE IDEA: there is only ONE REAL EXISTENCE — GOD; everything else is a MANIFESTATION / 'self-disclosure' (tajalli) of that divine reality. The phenomenal world is God's mirror; the mystic's goal is to realise this unity by extinguishing his ego in God (FANA FIL ALLAH). STRIKING parallel to Advaita Vedanta's 'Brahman alone is real; the world is Maya' + 'Tat Tvam Asi' — a major reason Sufism + Bhakti movement had fruitful dialogues in medieval India. Dara Shikoh (Shah Jahan's eldest son, executed by Aurangzeb in 1659) wrote MAJMA-UL-BAHRAIN ('Confluence of Two Oceans') comparing Sufi + Vedantic ideas, + translated UPANISHADS into Persian (SIRR-I-AKBAR, 1657 — this Persian version reached Europe and influenced Schopenhauer). COMPETING DOCTRINE: WAHDAT-USH-SHUHUD ('Unity of Witness') — proposed by Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi (Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, 16th-17th c.); held that the unity is PERCEPTUAL (the mystic SEES only God everywhere) but creator-creature distinction REMAINS. This was Orthodox Naqshbandi Sufis' corrective against Wahdat-ul-wujud, which orthodox ulema found heretical. AURANGZEB's religious orthodoxy was influenced by Sirhindi's school; DARA SHIKOH's syncretism by Ibn Arabi's.

questions.stem: The SUFI practice of 'SAMA' refers to:

options.option_text: Listening to MUSIC + devotional song as a means of attaining ecstatic union with God; central to Chishti practice; origin of QAWWALI

questions.explanation: SAMA (Arabic 'listening') — the Sufi spiritual practice of listening to devotional POETRY + MUSIC as a means to attain HAAL (ecstatic state) + WAJD (religious ecstasy) + ultimately FANA (annihilation of self in God). Essential to the CHISHTI order; its presence distinguished Chishtis from more orthodox orders. Condemned by strict ulema (who argued music is haram). EVOLVED into QAWWALI — the distinctive genre of Sufi devotional music in India, pioneered by AMIR KHUSRAU at the dargah of Nizamuddin Auliya. QAWWALI ELEMENTS: (1) group of singers called a qawwal party led by the main qawwal; (2) harmonium + tabla + dholak + hand-clapping; (3) call-and-response structure; (4) builds to ecstatic intensity; (5) Hamd (praise of Allah) → Naat (praise of Prophet) → Manqabat (praise of saints/Imams) → Ghazal (love themes, often with spiritual allegory) → Tarana (vocal acrobatics). FAMOUS QAWWALS: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan (died 1997), Sabri Brothers (Ghulam Farid + Maqbool Ahmed — 'Bhar Do Jholi'), Rahat Fateh Ali Khan, Warsi Brothers, Wadali Brothers, Kailash Kher (fusion). Famous qawwalis: 'Man Kunto Maula', 'Allah Hoo', 'Chaap Tilak', 'Aaj Rang Hai', 'Damadam Mast Qalandar' (about Lal Shahbaz Qalandar of Sehwan Sharif). Bollywood adaptation: 'Kun Faya Kun' (Rockstar 2011); 'Piya Haji Ali'. CHISHTI SHRINES in India, esp. Ajmer + Nizamuddin Delhi, have weekly sama sessions — pilgrims gather to listen + enter mystical states.

questions.stem: SHAIKH SALIM CHISHTI, to whose blessings Akbar attributed the birth of his son Jahangir (Salim), had his shrine located at:

options.option_text: FATEHPUR SIKRI — the white marble tomb inside the Jama Masjid complex; one of Mughal architecture's earliest white-marble masterpieces

questions.explanation: SHAIKH SALIM CHISHTI (1478-1572) — a 16th-century Chishti Sufi saint of Sikri (a village near Agra). REGAL CONNECTION: Emperor AKBAR (1556-1605), childless despite multiple queens, visited Salim Chishti in 1569 seeking blessings for an heir. The Shaikh's blessings were believed to have resulted in the birth of JAHANGIR (born 30 August 1569 in Sikri) — NAMED SALIM after the saint. In gratitude, AKBAR MOVED HIS CAPITAL from Agra to Sikri, and renamed it FATEHPUR SIKRI ('City of Victory') — served as capital 1571-85 (abandoned due to water scarcity). TOMB of Salim Chishti — built 1581 during Akbar's reign, initially of red sandstone; later REBUILT in pure white marble by Jahangir (one of the earliest Mughal white-marble tombs, a precursor to the Taj Mahal). EXQUISITELY CARVED JAALIS (stone lattices) — widely celebrated. PILGRIMAGE: childless couples visit + tie SACRED THREADS on the jaalis praying for offspring. Located inside FATEHPUR SIKRI's JAMA MASJID complex; access through BULAND DARWAZA ('Lofty Gate', built 1575 by Akbar after his Gujarat conquest — at 54m tall, one of the highest gateways in the world, bears Quranic inscription referring to Jesus). UNESCO World Heritage Site (Fatehpur Sikri, 1986). Other Fatehpur Sikri buildings: Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas (with the central pillar), Jodha Bai's palace, Ibadat Khana (religious debate hall).

questions.stem: Which Sufi saint's teachings strongly influenced GURU NANAK, with 134 of his verses appearing in the GURU GRANTH SAHIB?

options.option_text: BABA FARID (Sheikh Fariduddin Ganjshakar) — 12th-13th-c. Chishti saint of Pakpattan, Punjab; whose compositions form the largest non-Sikh Guru section of Guru Granth Sahib

questions.explanation: BABA FARID — FARIDUDDIN MASUD GANJSHAKAR (c. 1173-1266) — one of the first Punjabi SUFI POETS + a major Chishti saint. DISCIPLE of Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki; in turn Nizamuddin Auliya's spiritual GRANDMASTER + Baba Farid chose Nizamuddin as his successor. BASED at Pakpattan (then Ajodhan) in Punjab (now Pakistan). HIS 134 VERSES (SHLOKAS / SALOKS) — composed in early PUNJABI — are included in the GURU GRANTH SAHIB (the Sikh holy scripture) by Guru Arjan in 1604. This is the LARGEST non-Sikh-Guru contribution to the Granth — showing how deeply Baba Farid influenced early Sikhism through Guru Nanak's devotion. HIS PUNJABI poetry laid the foundation of Punjabi literature. THEMES: the transience of life, poverty, humility, love of God. FAMOUS line: 'Nanga aya nanga chalega' ('You came naked and will leave naked'). NAME 'GANJSHAKAR' ('treasure of sugar') — per legend, in his extreme fasting his mouth would even taste salt as sugar due to his sweetness of devotion. FARIDKOT city in Punjab named after him. His URS is a major event in Pakpattan (Oct-Nov). BULLEH SHAH (1680-1757), Waris Shah (Heer Ranjha), + Shah Hussain are later Punjabi Sufi poets influenced by Baba Farid's tradition. Pakistani Coke Studio features many Baba Farid kalams.

questions.stem: Match the Sufi order with its chief Indian centre: (1) CHISHTI; (2) SUHRAWARDI; (3) NAQSHBANDI; (4) QADIRI.

options.option_text: AJMER + Delhi; MULTAN; SIRHIND; Uch Sharif + Lahore (later Aurangabad)
Kashmir only; Lahore only; Delhi; Bihar

questions.explanation: FOUR MAJOR SUFI SILSILAS in medieval India, with chief centres: (1) CHISHTIYA — Introduced by KHWAJA MOINUDDIN CHISHTI (Ajmer, 1190s). Key centres: AJMER (Moinuddin), DELHI (Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki, Nizamuddin Auliya, Chirag-e-Dilli), PAKPATTAN (Baba Farid), Fatehpur Sikri (Salim). Characteristic: poverty, sama (music), open to all, rejected state patronage. (2) SUHRAWARDIYA — Introduced by BAHAUDDIN ZAKARIYA (d.1262) at MULTAN; orthodoxy-friendly; accepted state patronage + wealth. Other centre: Uch Sharif; Makhdoom Jahanian Jahangasht. (3) NAQSHBANDIYA — introduced by KHWAJA BAQI BILLAH (1564-1603) at Delhi; later centred at SIRHIND under SHAIKH AHMAD SIRHINDI ('Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani' / 'Revivalist of the Second Millennium', 1564-1624), who opposed Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi + advocated strict sharia; criticised wahdat-ul-wujud in favour of wahdat-ush-shuhud. Influential on Aurangzeb. (4) QADIRIYA — founded globally by Abdul Qadir Jilani (Baghdad, 12th c.); in India brought to UCH SHARIF + LAHORE by Sayyid Muhammad Ghaus + Sayyid Bandagi (15-16th c.); later centre in AURANGABAD. DARA SHIKOH (Shah Jahan's son) was a Qadiri Sufi — wrote Sakinat-ul-Auliya, Safinat-ul-Auliya. OTHER smaller silsilas: SHATTARI (popularised by Muhammad Ghaus in Gwalior; Mian Tansen of Akbar's court was a Shattari).

questions.stem: 'DIN-I-ILAHI' ('Divine Faith'), a syncretic religious movement combining elements of Islam, Hinduism, Jainism, Zoroastrianism + Christianity, was founded by:

options.option_text: AKBAR (in 1582, at Fatehpur Sikri's Ibadat Khana)

questions.explanation: DIN-I-ILAHI ('Religion of God') — a syncretic religious movement propounded by AKBAR in 1582 CE. CONTEXT: Akbar, greatly influenced by Sufi thought (Chishti) + Hindu + Jain + Parsi + Christian ideas, held inter-religious debates at the IBADAT KHANA ('House of Worship') built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575. Scholars from different faiths were invited — Portuguese Jesuits (Monserrate, Aquaviva), Parsi priests (Meherji Rana), Jain monks (Hiravijaya), Hindu Brahmins (Purushottama), Sufi mystics, Sunni + Shia ulema. Out of these debates Akbar issued the 'Mahzar' declaration (1579) making himself the Mujtahid (supreme interpreter). In 1582 he promulgated DIN-I-ILAHI. FEATURES: strict MONOTHEISM (TAWHID); rejected caste; preached ethical life (no meat; no marriage with aged/child; respect for animals; sun salutations; evening-prayer to light); membership voluntary, open to all; Akbar himself was 'spiritual guide'. NOT imposed. FOLLOWERS: barely 18-19 courtiers — RAJA BIRBAL (the most prominent), Abul Fazl, Faizi. DECLINE: died out soon after Akbar's death (1605); never had mass appeal; not a proper 'religion' but more a philosophical order. BACKLASH: (a) SHAIKH AHMAD SIRHINDI (Naqshbandi) emerged as sharp critic, rallying orthodoxy; (b) Badauni, Akbar's historian, was privately hostile (read Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh). AKBAR ALSO abolished jizya (1564) + pilgrimage tax (1563); married Rajput princesses (Jodha Bai / Hira Kunwari from Amber); promoted Rajputs to highest offices. SULH-I-KUL ('universal peace') was Akbar's broader doctrine.

questions.stem: The NIZAMUDDIN DARGAH complex in Delhi (13th-century Chishti shrine) contains the tombs of several famous persons. Which of these is NOT buried there?

options.option_text: DARA SHIKOH — actually buried in HUMAYUN'S TOMB (some sources say just a marker; site remains unidentified)

questions.explanation: NIZAMUDDIN DARGAH COMPLEX (Nizamuddin West, Delhi) — the shrine of Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya (1238-1325), 4th great Chishti saint. DESIGNED by medieval Chishti architecture; shrine built 1562 during Humayun's reign. NOTABLE GRAVES in the complex: (1) HAZRAT NIZAMUDDIN AULIYA — saint's grave (under white marble + red sandstone chattri). (2) AMIR KHUSRAU — closest disciple of Nizamuddin; buried a few metres from his master per his own wish. (3) JAHANARA BEGUM (1614-1681) — Shah Jahan's eldest daughter, herself a Sufi (Qadiriyya) — buried adjacent to her master Nizamuddin Auliya's tomb per her will ('no marble, only grass be my shroud'). (4) MIRZA GHALIB (1797-1869) — Urdu + Persian poet; his tomb is in the Ghalib Qabristan, a separate enclosed compound just to the south of the dargah (not in the main shrine premises, but within the complex). (5) Atgah Khan (Akbar's foster father, murdered by Adham Khan). (6) Muhammad Shah Rangeela (Mughal emperor 1719-48). (7) Inayat Khan (jewel merchant). DARA SHIKOH (1615-1659), Shah Jahan's eldest son, was EXECUTED by Aurangzeb in 1659; his body was buried in HUMAYUN'S TOMB complex in an unmarked grave (some historians say Grave 14 there; others say unidentified). Was himself a Qadiri Sufi + scholar (translated Upanishads as Sirr-i-Akbar). MODI GOVT in 2020 set up committee to identify Dara Shikoh's grave — unresolved. ANNUAL URS at Nizamuddin = huge gathering; QAWWALI every Thursday evening in the courtyard.
